notes.title: Patch notes for 2023-Oct-10
notes.content:
[h1]Version 1.57.1010[/h1]

This is the first post-launch patch that’s mostly comprised of small fixes. Because I will be taking a much needed vacation soon, I want to get this out to everyone sooner than later! Thanks! :)

[h2]UI[/h2]
[list]
[*] Save Menu missing OpenDyslexic font for “Save to Empty Slot” fixed
[*] Adjusted buttons on main menu
[*] Other small UI fixes
[*] Animations on hack buttons now active
[/list]

[h2]Narrative and images[/h2]
[list]
[*] Chloe’s role in the Codex has been updated
[*] Fixed the transparent back of Torrent’s head in one of the sprites
[*] Typos in 1.1 has been fixed
[*] Clarified when flashbacks end in 1.1 and adjusted the film grain post-processing
[*] Sueli is now more pleased with Chloe if she converts [redacted] to the cause in 2.3
[*] Frederick expression changes in 2.8
[*] Multiple characters’ expression changes in 3.3 
[*] Fixed distortion of crowd characters in 4.2
[*] Hakim expression changes in 4.5
[/list]

[h2]Controls[/h2]
[list]
[*] Continue game button can no longer be interacted with while it’s offscreen when returning to main menu from game (thank you PollyPlushie for finding this bug!)
[/list]

[h2]Known issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] Holo projector fx is not applying to Niallis in 2.2, nor in 2.9 and 4.5
[*] Audio issue of some sounds fading out or ambience sounding quieter when they’re not supposed to
[*] Exiting Chloe's Thoughts UI via B button while it is animating and reopening duplicates Chloe's thoughts. This does not crash the game nor soft locks it, and is just a UI visual error.
[*] Rare bug: Truck in 4.5b goes missing in one node if you make a save in a particular spot in the game. 
[*] Rare bug: Car in 4.7 duplicates if you make a save in a particular spot in the game.
[*] Very Rare bug: In less than 1/30 chances, controller LB + RB simultaneous button press during some hacks may cause tooltips to open rather than allow player to select a hack choice.
[/list]

notes.title: Solace State: Gayming Live and upcoming livestreams!
notes.content:
[h2]Solace State is at Gayming Live![/h2]
Solace State is part of the Gayming LIVE Indie Showcase from NOW until Oct 14th!

Director Tanya Kan will be running her own livestream about the dev process 
[h3]Sunday Oct 8 at 1:30PM ET![/h3]

Join the Vivid Foundry livestream on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/vividfoundry]Twitch.tv[/url]! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/efa5b4d6ae89c0ce138ea7eb43bc424775b7ab17.jpg[/img]

[h2]Previously at Game Devs of Color Expo[/h2]
We just enjoyed an amazing [url=https://www.gamedevsofcolorexpo.com/]Game Devs of Color Expo[/url] the past week! Seamus Ly (Generalist Developer of Solace State) and I (Tanya Kan, Director and Executive Producer) did a talk entitled "[b]Queer Advocacy in Indie Game Design: A Solace State Retrospective[/b]" where we talked about how our narrative design around choice building social trust is structured, and what political science research inspired the game.

I also organized another Game Devs of Color talk with Nana Moon (Keylocker, Virgo Versus The Zodiac) and Sherveen Uduwana (Midautumn) called “[b]Transformative Roles and Culture in Queer Fantasy and Sci-Fi Games[/b]”. We talked about authenticity as well as change, for both our game characters and for ourselves as devs!

Because these are ticketed events, we'll let you know when the recordings become available - likely sometime next year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/4e86310dbe67d9cac94d9b564edc3555c37d31bb.jpg[/img]

[h2]VODs on Youtube[/h2]
Solace State's team has had lots of livestreams and recordings over the years. Tanya will be gradually uploading both new and old content over the next months.
Click [url=https://www.youtube.com/@vividfoundry]here[/url] to follow our Youtube channel! 

[h2]Review: A cyberpunk story closer to home[/h2]
After a full playthrough of Solace State, Frank Sanchez called the game "a can't-miss topical thought exercise and more, given current news and events in 2023".
Read his full game review [url=https://thelowkeygeek.substack.com/p/a-cyberpunk-story-closer-to-home]here[/url]! 

[h2]The rest of the year in development[/h2]
We’re delighted by how stable the game is on launch! The biggest bug to fix is sound-related but do not impact the game's stability.​

As the temperatures drop, we will be looking at bringing the game to itch.io and improving Steam Deck performance!

If you like our game, please consider leaving us a review! Your support keeps our independent, experimental, provocatively diverse studio alive. Thank you!

notes.title: A team interview with Seamus Ly - Generalist Developer on Solace State!
notes.content:
As Solace State gears up for our game release next month, we will be sharing with you developer interviews, blog posts, and more sneak peeks of our game! 

[h1]Let's jump into an interview with Seamus Ly[/h1]
He's been working on Solace State since late summer 2021, and he's deep-dived into everything from level design with some really tight camera work, to programming post-processing systems, audio systems, and input systems with controllers! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/87cbd6bdf69f38735f545c61d112860c111d84e6.png[/img]

[b]Tanya Kan (Director)[/b]: Welcome, Seamus! What are some of the things that you've been working on this year? No spoilers, of course.

[b]Seamus Ly (Generalist Developer)[/b]: During the spring, I was doing VFX and animation in some more intense scenes. There's level design to do, art for UI and *other stuff*. During both spring and summer, there's a lot of bug-fixing as well, usually code and level-related. There's a lot of different facets of development I work on, but I enjoy it!

[b]TK[/b]: What's something that you have done on this game that you have never done in your previous work before? What is something you would tell a beginner programmer about learning something challenging, especially when working with other folks on the team?

[b]SL[/b]: I didn't do a lot of tools programming until working on Solace State. I've created tools for audio and VFX implementation. In other places, I've adapted what was already there, done by a previous dev. Something that's really important when you know other people are going to look at your work to is *comment your code*. 

I think a lot of beginner devs who are used to being solo programmers tend to fall into the pitfall of not properly documenting or commenting code. There's this feeling of "I made it, I'll always know how it works." But the you who exists a few months from when you close that task, and your co-worker who might have to fix something associated with it will absolutely thank you. Definitely something you want to get into the habit of doing.

[b]TK[/b]: What's your favorite part of Solace State development? 

[b]SL[/b]: Being a generalist has been an incredible learning experience. I started off doing UI layouts and working on shaders, which I had virtually no experience with at the time. I moved to level design and programming later, and I think they've become my easily favourite part of dev.

There are a few chapters of the game that I worked on the level design and animations of that I'm very fond of. I hope you'll enjoy them as much as I enjoyed working on them! 😉 ✨

[b]TK[/b]: Ooh, I'm especially excited about that fast-paced scene you've level design featuring speed hacker Torrent! You also worked on downtime scenes which players can get to know some characters, romantically if they wish! Can't wait for launch so that players can experience them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/b2f15f7bec7ae6060ba46c5373893e900df1e9a6.gif[/img]

Yeah, wow, what a breadth of development work that you've covered since summer 2021! You've been working on UI, shaders, and camera effects a lot more lately! How did you find stepping up to the challenge?  

[b]SL[/b]: I needed a lot of help at first, and I did a lot of research. It helped that I was able to ask for support on some things from other team members. Another important lesson for junior devs is that it is absolutely okay for you to not have all the answers to a task at first.

Be confident in your skills but be honest when you're uncertain about something. Your co-workers will absolutely be there to help when you need it. That's how I started almost 2 years ago now on Solace State. So, keep working at it!

I have since made the hack ID shaders that Chloe uses when she's iconohacking, and worked on overhauling menus, so I have gotten a lot more confident in my abilities over the years! You don't have to be perfect starting out and you'll make it to where you want to be with time!

[b]TK[/b]:  Yes! Love that good advice. You're great at communicating complex design & programming, and that's super nice on a gamedev team!  

Here's the cool hack ID shader you made that Chloe's applied onto Torrent while they're intervening in a violent situation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/575ca7a170101ec5e378fe66d79723b9517131ed.gif[/img]

[b]TK[/b]: You have experience in working on both video games and tabletop games, including PC dating visual novel ValiDate and tabletop games with Monte Cook Games. How do tabletop games help you with designing video games?

[b]SL[/b]: I find that writing for TTRPGs means taking all the different avenues of player choice into account. In a TTRPG, players can do basically anything. I've definitely been blindsided as a GM by decisions players have made in the past. 

So, when I write stories for games or design mechanics, I tend to think of what options do I think a player would want here. Should there be a direct route to problem-solving? Should there be something more roundabout for people who want to be clever about their solutions? 

Also, I'm always considering space and how best to convey how much space players have in an environment, because that can be crucial to some decisions. Of course, you can't always offer *every* avenue to your players in a video game, but it's interesting to consider when you're making choice-based, non-linear games.

[b]TK[/b]: I love that there's different ways to funnel expectations and choices in both types of games; They're fun design challenges! 

Who is your favorite Solace State character? Or characters, if you've got multiple favorites! 

[b]SL[/b]: It's so hard to choose, honestly! I'm a big Torrent fan. I really connect with him, and he's just got a lot of charming little traits that make him a well-rounded character.

And this character hasn't been discussed much on socials yet, but Raylene is also a favourite of mine as I've been working through chapters that feature her more as of late. All I'll say is, she's got a lot of complexity that I missed my first few times playing the game myself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/c564d71729c40af386892a1e7fcbbb9fa1867612.png[/img]

[b]TK[/b]: Oooh, even I didn't know you're excited about Raylene, haha. She's such a delightful character for me to write! I'm glad you like her.

What's one part of Solace State development, design, or programming which is much more complex than it may appear to most players?

[b]SL[/b]: Definitely the design. Aside from the complexity of how we handle narrative implementation (of which Technical Narrative Designer Sunny does a great job), the moving parts of VFX, animation, and character and camera placements are all things you have to consider when setting up a scene.

It's wonderful when it all comes together though! 💪

[b]TK[/b]: Right? Because we went with a 3D world and a custom camera system, everything has to be handcrafted! And thank you to Sunny for being so patient with so many branching story paths!   

What's one story arc that really resonates with you in Solace State?

[b]SL[/b]: I'm bringing up the boy again, but Torrent's story is one of my favourites. Without spoiling much, and as seen in past demos, Torrent's got a complex family dynamic. That's something I think a lot of people can relate to, regardless of where the conflicts may come from.

I can't talk about it, but I personally was satisfied with how it ended up turning out. I'm glad that the game's narrative is one that allows Torrent the time to navigate those issues. And I like how optimistic he is through everything without being naive. He's very mature! 

[b]TK[/b]: Thanks so much Seamus! You're such an amazing person to work with! We can't wait for the game to come out so that everyone can see your hard work! 

[h1]What else have we been working on?[/h1]
[list]
[*] A lot of playtesting and bug fixes since the start of the year (1000+ bug fixes tracked!)
[*] Progress in reaching cert for Xbox!
[*] Adding accessibility functionality, including applying OpenDyslexic font to everything in-game 
[*] Narrative fixes for those 200,000+ words and making sure that all the choices get tracked
[*] Partaking in events like Steam Visual Novel Festival, LudoNarraCon, Access-Ability Summer Showcase, and more!
[/list]

[b]If you missed it, here's our announcement trailer from last month: [/b]

[previewyoutube=qgXrF2-GZm0;full][/previewyoutube]

By the way, we're already working on our launch trailer! We're so excited! 
Stay tuned for more announcements! You can get updates and chat with us on [url=https://discord.gg/vividfoundry]Discord[/url]!

notes.title: Tuesday, March 28: Solace State Storytelling Stream! Storytellers Festival 2023
notes.content:
[h1]What is the Storytellers Festival?[/h1]

We're thrilled to announce that we'll be participating in the Storytellers Festival on Steam, an amazing event celebrating the art of narrative game and visual novel developers! From March 25th to April 1st, join us in exploring the wonderful world of storytelling in gaming! 


During the festival, our updated demo (maybe one of our last ones before we launch!) will be available for free download, so be sure to check it out while you can. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/3c5b98bdeee3c48b74684f9c3e91145e2ecf7a05.png[/img]

[h1]Our livestream:[/h1]


Additionally, we'll be hosting a live stream on Steam on [b]Tuesday, March 28 at 7pm ET (4pm PT)[/b] to delve deeper into our game's characters, plot, and unique storytelling style. Join us then to talk with our devs live!

This will be a dev-packed event because 5 Solace State devs will be in attendance and talking about many aspects of narrative design, game writing, and character development! Bring your questions and enjoy! 


[h1]Dev updates: [/h1]
While we’re at it, we should tell you that we’ve been busy this month with fixing bugs and building some expanded scenes in narrative edits and level design! Because our mix of 2D-3D systems is built in such an unusual way, we have to take care to test and make sure that the game plays as we intended! 


[h1]✨How to watch and chat✨[/h1]
Lots of people aren’t used to live streams on Steam! Just go to our store page at the designated time, and our live broadcast should pop up! Click “Show chat” to participate :)

Go support others too! We will give you a link to the Storytellers Festival when it goes live on March 25th at 1pm! 


Don’t forget to play our limited-time demo during the event via our store page. It’s totally free to download and play until [strike]Saturday April 1st at 11:59PM ET[/strike]! Actually, we will extend the availability of the demo by making it available until Monday April 3rd at 11:59PM ET! Happy gaming!

Want to chat with us more, during and after the livestream?[url=https://discord.gg/solacestate] Join our Discord here[/url]!

notes.title: Feb 2023's ~mysterious~ Solace State updates! Our press coverage & more!
notes.content:
You haven’t heard from us in a while (because we’ve been super heads-down on finishing up our game!) but this is indie game Solace State, a cyberpunk visual novel about friendship, civic duty, and the biotech revolution.

We are SO excited to announce that our game will be released on Xbox and Steam later this year!

Here’s our latest trailer to get you as pumped as we are:

[previewyoutube=fd6LrTJ7wAQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Dev Progress
[/h1]
We’ve added lots of polish in our artwork, including even more character art and environment art for our thriving metropolis! Did you know that the game now has 31 fully illustrated characters? Chloe, our main character, has 58 poses and counting!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/74bb9508b1efbe120922345a8a143388cfde5444.png[/img]

Extra polish also means improved accessibility by using OpenDyslexic font and character highlights to show who's talking, 50 save slots (wooow!), and getting everything ready to port over to Xbox!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/d483c857034de7b3cb71d47490370ef4b0ed5e4d.png[/img]

[h1]Four-tunate Press![/h1]
We’re so honoured that Solace State has been featured in four articles recently. Check them out:
[list]
[*][url=https://kotaku.com/2023-indie-game-release-date-roundup-pc-ps5-xbox-switch-1849960941/slides/21]Kotaku: 30 Indie Games You Should Know About Releasing in 2023[/url]
[*][url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/ileanadugato/here-are-30-lgbtq-video-games-being-released-in-2023-to]Buzzfeed: Here Are 30 LGBTQ Video Games Being Released In 2023 To Look Forward To[/url]

notes.title: Solace State's 2021 Roundup!
notes.content:
[h2]"Hello, world!"[/h2]

Despite a year when challenges seemed more insurmountable than ever, Solace State’s development went full steam ahead! Solace State in 2021 has seen more production development from both myself and our larger team than in any previous year. In fact, those of you who have played our last demo might notice how far it’s come even in the sample screenshots below!

My name is Tanya Kan, and I’ve been working on Solace State as the video game’s Director for years. I’m a studio owner who balances administration and marketing with development work, which includes leading in writing, art direction, 3D art, game design, and level design. 

And I’m making this game so much bigger than what I initially anticipated, because I need to tell this story about a young woman coming to grips with how her personal anguish has a political root. It’s about her journey to find herself in a community and to move away from wholesale apathy, all while really gaining ownership over the choices that she can make.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/b2f15f7bec7ae6060ba46c5373893e900df1e9a6.gif[/img]

Of course, you as the player will be able to likewise gain ownership over her journey within our choice-driven narrative. Below, the player makes a choice for Chloe when meeting Torrent for the first time.

None of us exist in a bubble away from politics, health, art, and work, so all my life I’ve never separated these spheres from each other, and made politics and health my art’s key themes. 

Creating this narrative feels like distilling and bottling up a bit of hope for now, and for later. I hope you enjoy reading what we’ve been up to for now, and get excited with what’s to come.

[h2]Team[/h2]

As for Solace State’s core development, our team has gotten larger since the beginning of 2020, bringing five additional specialists to help with Solace State’s production pipeline. And everyone brings with them unique perspectives and experiences. I learn something new weekly from the most junior to the most senior person!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/b1144b6f2d7423161a140302263922666a2948f0.jpg[/img]

[h2]Character Complexity and Art[/h2]

The narrative now has over 30 characters with narrative lines and character art. We also added in a new main character, Sueli, who has both her own character arc as an experienced community leader, and can be Chloe’s potential love interest. Sueli was uniquely challenging to me as a writer at first, because I’ve lived with the story of Chloe, Rebecka, Torrent, and Alden and how they intertwine for years. But now, I cannot imagine how Solace State could possibly work without Sueli too. 

Here’s a cute comic of Sueli! For more Solace State comics, be sure to join our [url=https://discord.gg/solacestate]Discord[/url] and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/SolaceStateGame]Twitter[/url] for more! If you want to see us create more comics, please give us a nice comment! <3

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/d4cacc2c45a1422e522cd01aff68c1fedfba0c44.png[/img]

We’ve expanded a lot more narrative nuance into how different characters experience gradual autocratic control, including through increased militarization, misinformation, and crackdowns. 

We also improved on a lot of character art rendering, so that the camera can pull in tighter to give you those deeply emotional shots of the character’s expressions. This is combined with a lot of large 3D neighborhoods for Chloe and her gang to explore. Much of the architectural modelling is already complete, though we are working on adding details, colors, and shaders to them to really make them pop. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/5f2ef13e634043005aeb7770edc5d3f75c6ec8d1.png[/img]

[h2]Visual Novel Presentation[/h2]

Speaking of legibility, after some testing, we made the speech bubbles ADV style so that it’s much easier to read for hours on end (ADV style is the more typical UI design style of having a screen-space text box at the bottom of the screen). Previously, 3D speech bubbles were rendered at an angle and limited our camera composition as well. The diegetic text and the transitioning cameras are still very much features we’re keeping, of course! 

[h2]Narrative[/h2]
Writing the entire narrative script is almost done, and there’s a part of my heart that shrieks at that, because how can a story be [i]done[/i]? But it will be, and it’s a warming feeling nowadays that, when I re-read through Solace State’s dialogue, I find myself enjoying it. I enjoy its whimsy, its self-reference, its allowance to let its characters breathe and live and make mistakes, and find joy.

We use Articy, an interactive storytelling management system to plug into Unity Engine for our branching story paths and many variables. This is just a small part of the larger picture!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/8931db728c3e47d4cc6c192491cd9c1605346149.png[/img]

[h3]Thank you for your continued support![/h3]

Healing from a difficult year also means reminding myself that I can have stress, but also moments of serenity. We are all actively trying our best! And I’ve got such a good team to remind me that I’m doing the best that I can, too.  

Shout-outs to our team members who have put in the most hours the past year in Solace State’s development: Gabi’s been working with so much nuance on Solace State as Lead Programmer that they predict many of my questions. Reilly, Character Artist, builds ample intention into each pose and outfit that she creates. Ashley, Writer, helped me reframe the narrative pacing, from our writing room meetings to her first drafts. Lauren, 3D Artist, dives into creating many neighborhoods’ architectural assets and its painterly style. Seamus and Sunny, newest to the team, have moved us forward by leaps and bounds on level design and narrative content integration respectively. And Jayme makes sure we stay focused and capable in taking on our responsibilities every week as Project Manager. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/ca9e3fcb9568baad06da906e5f194fce6e8c1688.png[/img]

Whenever I write, now and in the past, I’ve always circled around concepts of injustice and unfairness.

But perhaps the other thing I can’t help is to find the silver linings in every dark cave, and to make it into a conversation. And, what better way for Solace State to do that than through interactive storytelling driven by choice?

Peace and love, 
Tanya

tags.feature: We also added in a new main character, Sueli, who has both her own character arc as an experienced community leader, and can be Chloe’s potential love interest.

Speaking of legibility, after some testing, we made the speech bubbles ADV style so that it’s much easier to read for hours on end (ADV style is the more typical UI design style of having a screen-space text box at the bottom of the screen).
The diegetic text and the transitioning cameras are still very much features we’re keeping, of course!

notes.title: Solace State joins 2020 Steam Games Festival Summer Edition!
notes.content:
Solace State is an emotional 3D cyberpunk social hacking narrative game for PC on Steam and an unannounced console. You play as Chloe, a young hacker who seeks to reconnect with her friends in a militarized biotech state. Characters will remember how Chloe treats them intimately and in the broader political sphere, impacting how factions and cultures thrive or fall apart. 

We are sharing our [b]new time-limited demo[/b]—it’ll only be available to the public until the end of the Festival! The demo features a playable scene where your choices can impact a violent confrontation in a marginalized community and shift power dynamics. In playing the demo, you will discover parallels to complex, social issues of our times. We have new content since last month! The game demo is about 35 minutes long to play! 

[h3]Talk schedules[/h3]

On Tuesday June 16th at 7-9pm ET / 4-6PT, we will livestream new interviews with the team about the art and mechanics development, our recent Ubisoft Indie Series Grand Prize win, and a commented playthrough. Come chat with us! This is a Q&A, too! 

On Wednesday June 17th at 7-9pm ET / 4-6pm PT, we will [b]talk and amplify Black, Brown, and Indigenous writers[/b] on civil rights, philosophy, and grassroots movements. Our game is rooted in themes of people from all walks of life confronting the erosion of their rights, so we are amplifying how important these writers are to society and governance, and to Solace State’s narrative. As a studio with ethnically diverse and under-represented developers, we know that we must continually work against systemic racism and oppression.

[url=https://discord.com/invite/tU8JVQj][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/f9af8da4d6e19dd963f3db7a21581ccb5e4d6ee5.png[/img][/url]

Before, during, and after the event, you can always strike up a chat with our team on our Twitter or our Discord.

notes.title: Streaming new cyberpunk content for LudoNarraCon! 📺
notes.content:
While we’re all social distancing from home, the Solace State team will be attending the 2nd annual LudoNarraCon, and so can you!

[url=https://www.ludonarracon.com/]LudoNarraCon[/url] is an awesome online convention celebrating narrative games, and it’s hosted live right here on Steam! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/5c98cd4cbe22900a18b9c7b1362b0b7b01341a04.jpg[/img]

We’ll be talking about pretty much everything that goes into our development (besides spoilers of course🤫), including but not limited to:
[list]
[*] Our unique music-making process
[*] Designing game mechanics
[*] Lots of writing: Writing about sci-fi, politics, and romance in games!
[*] Lots of art too: character art, 3D art, and UI design!
[*] [b][i]And, of course we’ll be showing. New. In-game. Footage. Wooo![/i][/b]
[/list]

Catch our premiere live on [b]Friday, April 24th, starting at 10am PT (1pm ET)[/b]! 
Missed it? Our 4-hour exclusive content will be playing on Steam until Tuesday, April 28, 2020, 11:59pm PT (2:59am ET)! 

If you miss it, we won’t be able to answer your questions live, but a recording of our stream will be playing on loop until the convention is over.

We made this handy [url=https://t.co/sauEB7O1SJ?amp=1]Google Calendar invite[/url] for you so that you don’t forget😉

Before, during, and after the event, you can always strike up a chat with our team on our [url=https://twitter.com/solacestategame]Twitter[/url] or our [url=https://discord.gg/tU8JVQj]Discord[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/f9af8da4d6e19dd963f3db7a21581ccb5e4d6ee5.png[/img]

[h1]Limited time demo[/h1]

You know you want to experience revolutionary choices first-hand! Our demo of Solace State will be available for [b]a limited time from Friday April 24 9am PT until midnight PT on Friday May 1[/b]! This is the first time a demo is available on Steam, so don’t wait! 

[h1]Bonus Level: Panel Discussion[/h1]

On [b]Saturday April 25th at 12pm/noon PT[/b], our director Tanya Kan will also be participating on a live panel to discuss [b]personal storytelling in games[/b], with Paloma, Miriam, and Gabby! Click the image below to learn more:

[url=https://www.ludonarracon.com/panels][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33468288/15be9e755163538bbf054d8f01dc658dd6ab73ae.png[/img][/url]

Excited to chat with you all!
